tests.name: test_script
tests.description: The script's run: patience 2, and the losses 1.0, 0.8, 0.9, 0.85, 0.7.
tests.message: With patience 2 and the losses [1.0, 0.8, 0.9, 0.85, 0.7], step gave [False, False, False, False, False], not [False, False, False, True, False]. 0.9 and 0.85 are two losses in a row after the best, 0.8, and 0.7 is a new best.

tests.name: test_patience_one
tests.description: With patience 1, the first loss after a new best that is no new best stops the run.

tests.name: test_improving
tests.description: A run whose loss falls every time never stops.

tests.name: test_against_the_best
tests.description: A loss is compared with the best so far, not with the loss just before it.
tests.message: With patience 2 and the losses [1.0, 3.0, 2.0], step gave [False, False, False], not [False, False, True]: 2.0 is lower than 3.0, but not lower than the best, 1.0.

tests.name: test_equal_is_no_best
tests.description: A loss equal to the best so far is not a new best.

tests.name: test_count_starts_again
tests.description: A new best starts the count again.
tests.message: With patience 3 and the losses [5.0, 6.0, 7.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 7.0], step gave [False, False, False, False, False, False, False], not False six times and then True. 4.0 is a new best, so the count starts again after it, and only the third loss after it reaches 3.

tests.name: test_after_stop
tests.description: After saying True, a watcher goes on counting, and a new best still starts the count again.

tests.name: test_large_first
tests.description: The first loss is a new best, however large it is.

tests.name: test_two_watchers
tests.description: Two watchers keep their own best losses and their own counts.

tests.name: test_true_or_false
tests.description: step returns True or False.

tests.name: test_order
tests.description: The first layer in the list is applied first.

tests.name: test_three
tests.description: Each layer is applied to what the layer before it gave.

tests.name: test_empty
tests.description: With no layers, the input comes back as it was.

tests.name: test_functions
tests.description: A plain function is a layer too.

tests.name: test_nested
tests.description: A Sequential can be called with one argument, so it can be a layer of another.

tests.name: test_each_once
tests.description: Each call of the model calls each of its layers once.

tests.name: test_own_copy
tests.description: A later change to the caller's list leaves the model as it was.
tests.message: After model = Sequential(layers) and then layers.append(AddOne()), model(5) is 11, not 10: the model should keep a copy of the list, which the caller's change does not reach.

tests.name: test_separate
tests.description: Two models keep their own layers.

tests.name: test_add
tests.description: + makes a value holding the sum.

tests.name: test_mul
tests.description: * makes a value holding the product.

tests.name: test_parents
tests.description: A result's parents are the two values it was made from themselves, left one first.

tests.name: test_new_object
tests.description: + and * make a new value.

tests.name: test_inputs_unchanged
tests.description: + and * leave the values they combine as they were.

tests.name: test_no_parents
tests.description: A value made without parents has an empty list of its own.
tests.message: Value(1).parents and Value(2).parents are one and the same list. A default value is made once, when the def line runs, and shared by every call, as E1.4 found.

tests.name: test_given_parents
tests.description: parents passed in are kept as they are.

tests.name: test_chain
tests.description: a * b + a, worked out in the order of its tree.

tests.name: test_repr
tests.description: print shows a value as Value(data).

tests.name: test_sum
tests.description: The sum has the sums of the coordinates.

tests.name: test_unchanged
tests.description: Both vectors added are left as they were.
tests.message: After u + v, u is Vec(4, 6), not Vec(1, 2).

tests.name: test_new_object
tests.description: The sum is a new vector.
tests.message: u + v should be a new vector, not u or v itself.

tests.name: test_chain
tests.description: Three vectors added in a row.
tests.message: After a + Vec(2, 2) + Vec(3, 3), a is Vec(6, 6), not Vec(1, 1).

tests.name: test_twice
tests.description: A vector added to itself.
tests.message: After u + u, u is Vec(2, 4), not Vec(1, 2).

tests.name: test_script
tests.description: The script prints Vec(1, 2) Vec(3, 4) Vec(4, 6).
tests.message: The script printed 'Vec(4, 6) Vec(3, 4) Vec(4, 6)\n', not Vec(1, 2) Vec(3, 4) Vec(4, 6).
